transcript.title: Opening
transcript.text: Good morning Rushil Bhatia. Here is your daily news for Sunday, October 11. In today's briefing: top headlines, bhopal and madhya pradesh, business and markets, money, tax and personal finance, science and technology, development and policy, across india, around the world. Let's begin.

transcript.title: Top headlines
transcript.text: First, the stories leading the news this morning. New York Mayor Mamdani says companies like Netflix will now pay if you can't cancel. New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's Click-to-Cancel rule is now in effect, requiring businesses to let customers cancel subscriptions the same way they signed up. Enforced by the Department of Consumer and Worker Protection, it covers streaming services like Netflix, Amazon Prime and Disney+, as well as gym memberships. Violations carry civil penalties starting at $525 and possible refunds. New Yorkers can file complaints through a new online city portal. New York fire fundraiser topped $100,000; state AG seeks $71,539 in unpaid funds. Hailey Bodah, a young New Yorker, faced unimaginable loss when a fire claimed the lives of her father and four sisters. In the wake of this tragedy, generous relatives raised over $100,000 to help her. However, legal issues emerged regarding the management of the funds, with the New York Attorney General's office demanding the return of over $71,000. 'Stupid boy': England cricket legend Ian Botham reignites feud with Ben Stokes. England legend Ian Botham has reignited his feud with Ben Stokes, calling him a "stupid boy" and a "has-been" over England's Ashes preparations and retirement. Botham criticised the team's lack of practice matches and trip to Noosa after defeats. Stokes defended modern cricket's demands and hit back online, saying, "it's better to be a has-been than a never-been." Restrained, detained, contained: Clampdown foils stir, thousands confined to home. Unprecedented security arrangements from central Delhi to the borders, phalanxes of 35,000 police and paramilitary personnel and a virtual choke on metro services and trains foiled Cockroach Janta Party's march to Jantar Mantar on Saturday. California couple rebuilt old backyard railway; estate later sold for $8.5m. A luxurious estate in La Cañada Flintridge was recently sold for $8.5 million, attracting numerous potential buyers. The property includes a custom five-passenger garden railway that enhances its unique appeal and charm. Additionally, the house consists of six bedrooms, eight bathrooms, and a gourmet kitchen perfect for entertaining. Extensive outdoor features include a swimming pool, vegetable garden, and manicured landscapes recognized with multiple awards. Saudi Arabia says attack on Riyadh airport killed 12 and wounded more than 300. At least 12 people were killed and over 300 injured after a missile struck Saudi Arabia's King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on Saturday, Saudi Arabia's General Authority of Civil Aviation (GACA) said. James Patterson's $1.75M gift saved 467 school libraries. James Patterson initially pledged $1.25 million to support US school libraries but increased the donation to $1.75 million. This increase followed an overwhelming response from schools, revealing their pressing needs for resources. A total of 467 libraries benefited from the grants, funding books, technology, and repairs. The American Association of School Librarians recognized Patterson for his advocacy and financial contributions. SIR stir: 'Kashmir model' in Delhi, situation akin to Emergency, says opposition. Internet restrictions and arrests during Cockroach Janta Party-led anti-SIR protests in New Delhi triggered sharp political reactions Saturday, as J and K CM Omar Abdullah said the "Kashmir model" had reached the capital, PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti called the restrictions a reminder of Kashmir's 2019 lockdown, and CPM described the atmosphere as "akin to the Emergency". CJP protest: How government pre-empted 'plot to incite violence'. After an action-filled day in which Delhi Police and security forces thwarted plans of CJP and opposition parties, govt and security establishment seemed satisfied with how events panned out. Renée Zellweger bought Topanga ranch for $3.35m, sold it for $6.4m. Renée Zellweger's stunning Topanga ranch, acquired in 2015 and beautifully renovated, has hit the market for nearly $8 million. Spanning almost 10 acres, this Spanish-style estate boasts breathtaking mountain views and exclusive hiking trails. Previously sold for $6.4 million in 2021, the property is perfect for those seeking tranquility in Southern California, featuring an infinity-edge pool and meticulously landscaped outdoor areas, appealing to buyers looking for space and luxury. Nepal cuts 12 year wait, to declare those missing in flood 'dead' after 45 days. Nepal govt has reduced the waiting period for declaring people missing in disasters dead from 12 years to just 45 days, paving the way for families of 5,285 people, including at least 189 Indians who went missing in the Aug 26 floods, to obtain death certificates and pursue compensation, insurance and inheritance claims.
